The harbour reopens after the storm

By Aino Virtanen

The fishing boats returned to the inner harbour on Saturday morning, three days after the storm closed the port and pushed a line of broken ice against the breakwater.

Harbour master Jussi Lehtonen said the divers had checked every mooring chain before the gates were opened. "We lost two buoys and a section of the old pier, but the channel is clear and the lights are working again," he said.

The storm brought gusts of more than thirty metres per second to the outer islands, according to the meteorological institute, and left about four thousand homes without electricity for most of Thursday.

Ferries to the islands will run on a reduced timetable until Monday, when the repaired ramp at the eastern terminal is expected to carry vehicles again. Foot passengers can travel from the western quay from noon today.

Local businesses along the waterfront spent the weekend clearing debris. The owner of a small café near the market square said the water had reached the second step of the terrace, the highest she had seen in twenty years.

The city council will meet on Tuesday to discuss funding for a higher breakwater, a plan that has been debated for more than a decade. Engineers have warned that storms of this strength are becoming more frequent as the sea ice forms later in the winter.

Volunteers from the sailing club helped to recover small boats that had broken free during the night. Many of them were found along the beach to the south, some with only minor damage to their hulls and rudders.

Residents are asked to report any damage to public property through the city's website, and to stay away from the old pier until it has been inspected by the structural engineers later this week.
